It is our intention to return to make a permanent repair as soon as we can.  I'm sorry, but we can't give you a time for this at present. Please accept our sincere apologies for any inconvenience this may cause.

Steps.Message:
Hi, it's Talie from the messaging team at UK Power Networks. I understand how difficult it can be without power and the additional worries this can bring.

For both our business customers and those at home, we will work as quickly and safely as possible to restore supplies. If you need any additional support or have any concerns, please call us on 105 or tweet us @ukpowernetworks.

I will personally continue to keep you updated with our progress.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Talie at 17:37 - Thanks for your patience over today.

Our engineers have let us know that specialist teams have begun to arrive on site and are working to remove the tree from our cabling. To give them time to do this safely, the estimated time frame to restore your power is now between 23:00 and 00:00.

We're sorry this is taking longer than expected, and we'll continue to keep you up to date, but if any change to this time comes in from our staff I'll let you know as soon as we hear.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: We became aware of this power cut at 17:38. We’re sorry for any disruption this may have caused you. We didn’t know in advance there would be a power cut, but now that we know, our teams will do everything they can to get your power back quickly. Engineers in our control room have switched some customers power back on in your area. To get everyone’s power back on we may need to attend to investigate and make repairs. We’ll continue to update you until everyone’s power is back on.

Steps.Message:
Update at 11:35 - We can confirm that all power in the  Park Lane & Silfield Road  area should be back on. The outage was caused by overhead cables on the ground. Our engineers have now made these safe and restored power. 

We're sorry for the length of time you were without power; this is due to damage on our network as a result of the heavy rain from Storm Austen and Storm Boelo.

If your power isn't back on or you want to speak to us about anything, call us on 08003163105 free from landlines and mobiles.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
We're sorry if your power is still off. Due to the high winds and heavy rain from Storm Beolo impacting our network, we're dealing with more power cuts than usual.
 
Our staff are working 24/7 to help customers and fix these problems, though due to extra reports of damage and the difficult conditions, it's taking us longer to get everything repaired and the lights back on.
 
As a result of this. We are now estimating we'll restore your power between 15:30 and 16:30. This is not the message we want to send, but we want to provide you with realistic updates so you can plan ahead.
 
Sent by Kevin

Steps.Message:
Sent by Talie at 15:38 - We can now confirm that all power in the Forest Row RH18  area should be back on. Our engineers have diverted power around the overhead cable fault to get the majority of customers back on. However, due to the location and complexity of the issue, we have also used temporary generators to restore power to the last of the affected properties. This will provide power until our engineers plan in and safely complete the full repair, which may take a few days.

We're really sorry for any disruption this unexpected power cut caused. If your power isn't on or there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Our engineers are awaiting the arrival of our generators.

Although these will be temporary, engineers will still need to repair the issue before they can be removed and network power is resumed. Depending on the fault, it may take several days for our engineers to pinpoint the problem and plan in the work. The temporary generators will remain on site to provide power until we can locate the issue and restore the network back to normal running conditions.

If you'd like any further information, our team are always here to help. Sent by Simon at 14:50.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Simon at 11:58 - Our engineers have completed their investigations.

We're sorry to change the time frame and will let you know when they arrive.

Logs.Comment:
Sent by Simon at 09:56 - Thanks for your patience today. Our engineers have now repaired the overhead cable that had come down on the ground, and have deemed it safe to restore power back to all 39 properties in the Ashford TN27 area.

We're very sorry we had to turn your power off unexpectedly, and with so little warning. We usually provide much more notice if we can, but in a situation like this our first priority is the safety of the public and our staff.

We know that being without power can be especially difficult, so we're sorry for the outage. If your power is still off or if you have any questions, call our team on 08003163105.

Hi there. We've just had a shift change, so Simon, Jack, Kevin, Bev and Donny are now here to keep you updated with progress from our field teams.

We know it's frustrating being without power, but we wanted to assure you we're still here and as soon as we have some more information we'll update you again.

We're sorry if your power is still off. Due to the high winds and heavy rain from Storm Beolo impacting our network, we're dealing with more power cuts than usual.
 
Our staff are working 24/7 to help customers and fix these problems, though due to extra reports of damage and the difficult conditions, it's taking us longer to get everything repaired and the lights back on.
 
We think it's unlikely we will be able to restore your electricity tonight. We are now estimating we'll restore your power between 18:00 and 19:00. This is not the message we want to send, but we want to provide you with realistic updates so you can plan ahead.
 
Sent by Will at 01:56.

Sent by Simon at 15:11 - We can now confirm that all power in the Tunbridge Wells and Crowborough area should be back on. Our engineers have diverted power around the fault on our overhead network to get the majority of customers back on. However, due to the location and complexity of the issue, we have also used temporary generators to restore power to the last of the affected properties. This will provide power until our engineers plan in and safely complete the full repair, which may take a few days.

We're really sorry for any disruption this unexpected power cut caused. If your power isn't on or there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.

Sent by Simon at 10:14 - I wanted to reach out to say that our staff are doing everything they can to get your lights back on. Heavy rain and strong winds like we're experiencing with Storm Boelo can make things harder for our engineers, especially when trying to repair overhead cabling.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind and making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations, so if you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Sent by Talie at 16:13 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

We'll keep you updated with our progress.

Sent by Donny at 12:29 - Thanks for your patience today. Our engineers have now investigated the tree resting on overhead lines, and have deemed it safe to restore power back to all 445 properties in the Little Baddow and surrounding area as they were identified to be telecom lines.

We're very sorry we had to turn your power off unexpectedly, and with so little warning. We usually provide much more notice if we can, but in a situation like this our first priority is the safety of the public and our staff.

We know that being without power can be especially difficult, so we're sorry for the outage. If your power is still off or if you have any questions, call our team on 08003163105.

Steps.Message:
Sent by Talie at 16:22 - We can now confirm that all power in the Sevenoaks TN15 area should be back on. Our engineers have diverted power around the grounded overhead cable to get the majority of customers back on. However, due to the location and complexity of the issue, we have also used a temporary generator to restore power to the last of the affected properties. This will provide power until our engineers plan in and safely complete the full repair, which may take a few days.

We're really sorry for any disruption this unexpected power cut caused. If your power isn't on or there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: Sent by Simon at 15:23 - We're sorry for the disruption to your power today, especially for those who may be more vulnerable without the electric. For more information just click here: https://UKPN.short.gy/PSR If you have any further concerns or questions though, don't hesitate to call us free on 08003163105. We'll continue to keep you updated with our engineer's progress.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

Sent by Talie at 18:40 - I wanted to reach out to say that our staff are doing everything they can to get your lights back on. Heavy rain and strong winds like we're experiencing with Storm Boelo can make things harder for our engineers, especially when trying to repair overhead cabling.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind and making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations, so if you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Steps.Message:
Sent by Simon at 12:27 - Thanks for your patience today. Our engineers have now investigated the low overhead cables, and have deemed it safe to restore power back to all 450 properties in the Ashford TN26 area.

We're very sorry we had to turn your power off unexpectedly, and with so little warning. We usually provide much more notice if we can, but in a situation like this our first priority is the safety of the public and our staff.

We know that being without power can be especially difficult, so we're sorry for the outage. If your power is still off or if you have any questions, call our team on 08003163105.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

Our staff have found a potentially dangerous situation involving low hanging overhead cables so have responded as quickly as possible and asked our control room to turn power off to the area using our high voltage network. This is why a wide area has lost electricity.

Our field teams are working to fix the issue as quickly as possible, and we'll start diverting power back to affected homes as soon as they advise us it's safe. You may notice your lights going on and off as we work to get as much power restored as we can.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing, but we'll always try to give you the clearest information we have.

Sent by Talie at 14:10 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

Usually we would send more frequent updates, so we apologise that due to the bad weather we have been unable to text as often. Storm Boelo has impacted our network with heavy rain and high winds, and we're dealing with a larger amount of power cuts than usual. 

We know that being without power can be very worrying, so we're sorry for the outage. If your power isn't on, or if there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us any time on 08003163105.

Our engineers have now arrived on site in the Rochester ME3 area to investigate the cause of the voltage issues.

At the moment our time frame to have power back on is between 22:30 and 23:30, but once our staff have fully assessed the situation this could change. Depending on what they find, it's possible our time frame may need to change later.

We know that a power cut can be very disruptive; we understand this can greatly impact your daily activities and we want to support you however we can. If you have any concerns, our team are always here on 08003163105. Sent by Simon at 11:12.

What will happen next?

This outage affects multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you expect. We're arranging staff to attend ASAP, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting electricity. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to get as many customers back on as we can.

Once available, our engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, they will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will work to locate the issue and make repairs, which may take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing but we'll always give you the clearest information we have.

Sent by Donny at 13:49 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Based on an average for this kind of issue, our estimated time to have you back on is between22:00-23:00. 

We'll keep you updated with our progress, but in the meantime our team are always here to talk on 105 if you have any questions or concerns.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

We're arranging staff to attend ASAP, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting electricity. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to get as many customers back on as we can.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing but we'll always give you the clearest information we have.

They will also check smaller sites which run along our cabling route, these break our network down into smaller sections and can help pinpoint any possible problems.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

This outage affects multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you expect. We're arranging staff to attend ASAP, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting electricity. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to get as many customers back on as we can.

Once available, our engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, they will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will work to locate the issue and make repairs, which may take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing but we'll always give you the clearest information we have.

Update at 17:15 - We can confirm that all power in the Dover CT15 area should be back on. Our engineers had to turn off the power to make urgent network repairs.

We're sorry for the length of time you were without power; this is due to damage on our network as a result of the heavy rain from Storm Austen and Storm Boelo.

If your power isn't back on or you want to speak to us about anything, call us on 08003163105 free from landlines and mobiles.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Bev at 17:04 - Our engineers are on their way. At this point we think the issue is an overhead cable fault affecting 113 properties.

Specialist engineers from our control room are also working to divert power remotely, so it's possible your power could come back on at any point. We can't always restore everyone this way. That's why we're also sending staff to the area to check our equipment.

Every fault is different, so our time frames have to be estimated but currently we hope to have power back on between 22:30 and 23:30. We must stress that it may become necessary for this to change, depending on what our engineers find.

We'll keep you updated with our progress.

Steps.Message:
Sent by Talie at 18:33 - A last message from us, as we can now confirm that all power in the Maidstone ME17 area should be back on. The issue was caused by an overhead cable fault, which our engineers have now diverted power around and they are not expecting to have to turn power off again. 

Usually we would send more frequent updates, so we apologise that due to the bad weather we have been unable to text as often. Storm Boelo has impacted our network with heavy rain and high winds, and we're dealing with a larger amount of power cuts than usual. 

We know that being without power can be very worrying, so we're sorry for the outage. If your power isn't on, or if there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us any time on 08003163105.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

This outage affects multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you expect. We're arranging staff to attend ASAP, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting electricity. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to get as many customers back on as we can.

Once available, our engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, they will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will work to locate the issue and make repairs, which may take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing but we'll always give you the clearest information we have.
